fresh_source_evidence.fact: Current INSPIRE files were published 5 July 2026 and are replaced on the first Sunday of each month.
INSPIRE is supplied as GML using open standards and may be converted for GIS use.
HMLR polygon geometry is captured against British National Grid; reprojection from BNG to WGS84 can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a freehold subset and show indicative rather than definitive legal extent.
Each individual polygon has a separate Land Registry-INSPIRE ID and a registered title may contain several polygons.
National Polygon lifecycle fields include unique Poly_ID, Title_No, INSERT, UPDATE, Vers_No and Rec_Status.
Index polygons are updated when there is appropriate title activity or adjoining-title activity rather than by blanket review of every current registration.
LIDAR Composite DTM 1m covers about 99% of England and removes surface objects to model bare terrain.
The 2022 composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022 and metadata index catalogues identify which survey contributed at a location.
Where repeat surveys exist the newest best-resolution data is used; resampled data is bilinearly interpolated before merge.
DTM data is supplied as GeoTIFF in 5km OS National Grid tiles, in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn with OSTN15; input surveys have +/-15cm RMSE vertical accuracy.
The dataset lists WCS plus Metadata Survey Index WMS/WFS services, enabling value provenance and survey lineage to be checked separately.
OS Terrain 50 is a lower-resolution bare-earth DTM supplied in 10km by 10km tiles identified by the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
Terrain 50 grid supply contains 200 by 200 pixels at 50m spacing, centre-of-pixel heights to 0.1m, with GML and PRJ spatial-reference support files.
OS Terrain 50 provides GEMINI metadata nationally and per tile; per-tile XML metadata identifies the 10km tile and supports acquisition metadata such as flying date.
Terrain 50 grid and contours are interpolated from a source TIN; vegetation and supported structures are removed where needed to represent bare earth.
